summary.text:
A short two-month update — 1 April to 31 May 2026 — that does not carry a CFR, a maturity table, a liability benchmark or an MRP schedule, so the balance-sheet identity cannot be evaluated from it. What it does give us reconciles cleanly. Total borrowing was £520.296m at 3.28%: £485.296m PWLB at 3.21%, £30.000m market loans at 4.33%, £5.000m short-term at 4.10%. Our PWLB file ties exactly at £485,295,804 across 97 loans at 3.2092%. The GF/HRA split is £162.265m / £358.031m.

The live item is the £5m Dexia LOBO that was subject to an interest rate review in April 2026 and repaid rather than accept the revised rate. That is the third Dexia trigger we have read across the library: Kent had a £40m LOBO called in 2025/26, Tameside a £5m LOBO called for a 16 June 2026 option date and prepaid, and now Brighton and Hove. All three ended in repayment. Every Dexia rate-review event we have logged over the last year has closed the same way.

The other numbers worth carrying are the £35m new HRA PWLB drawn in the period at 4.69% for 3 years (in our file, priced today at a small +£442k premium because 4.69% is below where the 3-year curve sits now), and the annotation on the capital-programme chart saying revenue costs rise by £10m per annum to over £26m by 2029/30 — an increase of circa 60% across the MTFS. Investment outperformance against SONIA has compressed from +29-32bp across the halves of 2025/26 to +14bp now, consistent with sitting largely in MMFs.

officer.subject: Your Dexia £5m repayment — the third we've logged this year
officer.body:
Hi [NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's premature repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on Appendix 4 to your 16 July Cabinet. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. It's a short two-month update rather than a full outturn, so this is a shorter note than most.

A cross-check first: we hold all 97 of your PWLB loans, £485,295,804 at a weighted 3.2092%, which rounds to your Borrowing Summary line of £485.296m at 3.21% on the pound and on the basis point. The £35m HRA loan drawn in the period at 4.69% for three years is in that file too, sitting in the 2-5 year bucket.

The part of the appendix that stood out is the Dexia repayment. Your £5m LOBO went to interest-rate review in April and you took it out rather than accept the revised rate. That is the third Dexia rate-review or call event we've read this year — Kent had a £40m LOBO called in 2025/26 and Tameside a £5m called for a 16 June 2026 option date; both councils repaid. In every case where Dexia has moved on a LOBO in our library, the borrower has ended up repaying rather than rolling. That is not something any single council can see from its own file, and it is one of the few real patterns to have emerged from the last six months of reading. Dexia also still sits as a non-called holder at Newcastle, Oldham, Wiltshire and Gloucestershire — we watch those.

On the 4.69% for three years, our engine at yesterday's DMO fixing (notice 314/26 PM) prices it at a small premium — about £442k on the £35m — because 4.69% is below where the three-year certainty curve sits today. So the loan is now marginally in-the-money to hold. That number is indicative only; only the DMO can quote a binding premium. But the daily version of that calculation for your whole book is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis — same formula, banker's rounding, D+1 day count, the lot. On today's curve the file prices as an indicative net discount of about £124m against a £485m repayment balance, with 89 of the 97 loans below par; the four largest discounts are all the long-dated 1.32% – 1.67% loans in the fifty-year tail. Whether any of that is worth acting on depends on replacement cost, which we don't model.

The other line we'd carry forward is the annotation on the cost-of-capital chart — an extra £10m per annum by the end of the MTFS taking the total to over £26m, a c. 60% rise. The interactive liability benchmark on pwlbtoday.org shows the same picture from the other side: it is built on live data and is now moving through the sector as CIPFA works up updates to the Prudential and Treasury Codes.

On training, three fit Brighton and Hove: LOBO loans, given where the appendix leaves the remaining market book; Break costs and premature repayment, for the £124m indicative discount position; and our liability benchmark pathway, given the MTFS trajectory the chart describes. For members, Cabinet Member (Finance) is written for exactly the meeting this appendix went to. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
